# Connector

**Package** `telividb.connector.v1`

## Services

### `McpServers`

Manages the MCP servers this deployment may call.

| Method | Request | Response | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CreateMcpServer` | `CreateMcpServerRequest` | `McpServer` | Registers an MCP server. |
| `GetMcpServer` | `GetMcpServerRequest` | `McpServer` | Retrieves a single registration. |
| `ListMcpServers` | `ListMcpServersRequest` | `ListMcpServersResponse` | Lists registered servers. |
| `IntrospectMcpServer` | `IntrospectMcpServerRequest` | `IntrospectMcpServerResponse` | Connects and enumerates what the server exposes. Reports the raw capability set. No model is involved and nothing is applied: the text here is written by whoever runs that server, so feeding it to something that decides what to embed would be a prompt-injection surface where the injected instruction acts on this deployment's data. |
| `DeleteMcpServer` | `DeleteMcpServerRequest` | `McpServer` | Soft-deletes a registration. |

## Messages

### `McpServer`

A registered MCP server this deployment may call tools on.  Consuming an MCP server is an ordinary source, not a parallel ingest path: it emits the same record stream bulk import already consumes, inheriting jobs, checkpoints, resume and reject files rather than growing failure machinery of its own.

| Field | Type | # | Behavior | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | 1 | `IDENTIFIER` | Resource name of the server. |
| `display_name` | `string` | 2 | `REQUIRED` | Human-readable name. |
| `endpoint` | `string` | 3 | `REQUIRED` | Where to reach the server. |
| `embed_results` | `bool` | 4 | `OPTIONAL` | Whether results from this server may be embedded into the index. False unless an operator sets it deliberately, and that default is the security boundary rather than a convenience. Text a server returns is written by whoever runs that server; embedding it makes it retrievable memory that a later context assembly can pull into a window, where it steers the agent. Unlike a one-time schema review, that recurs on every call and persists. Nothing infers this. A classifier may propose the change and may never apply it — automatic movement is permitted only toward withholding. |
| `capability_digest` | `string` | 5 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | Digest of the capability set last introspected from this server. A source that silently gains or changes a tool is how ingest starts dropping data or accepting something it was never reviewed for. Comparing this is what detects drift. |
| `introspect_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 6 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When the server was last introspected. |
| `create_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 7 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When the server was registered. |
| `update_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 8 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When the registration was last modified. |
| `delete_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 9 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When the registration was soft-deleted, or unset while it is live. |
| `expire_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 10 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When a soft-deleted registration is purged and becomes unrecoverable. |
| `etag` | `string` | 11 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | Opaque value for optimistic concurrency on update. |

### `McpTool`

One tool a server exposes.

| Field | Type | # | Behavior | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tool` | `string` | 1 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | Name the server gives this tool. Attacker-controlled text: written by whoever runs the server, never by this deployment. It is displayed and filtered on, and it is never fed to a model that decides what to embed. |
| `description` | `string` | 2 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | Description the server supplies, carried verbatim. |
| `input_schema` | `string` | 3 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | JSON Schema for the tool's input, as the server published it. |
